rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: Can You Keep It?
card.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tuesday dinners are stopping. What will you tell Sam when he asks?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're eating at home. He doesn't need the club's business.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chef hasn't been paid. Would you tell him that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No. He's collecting gossip for his column. Leave the chef's name out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You spotted the risk. I've been covering the wages myself. Can I trust you with the receipts?

card.title: Can You Keep It?
card.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I withdrew my college application. Have you told Mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked. I said my sister's plans were hers to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then there's more. I've leased a bakery. Can I send you the address?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Call me. Mum uses my tablet; she'd see the message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. I'll call. It's Mum's old bakery. I want you there when I tell her.

card.title: Hand Over the Proof
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the actual note, not your description.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can read it to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want the words that don't get your emphasis.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's private.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me the one line you're using to decide for me.

card.title: Hand Over the Proof
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the drawer key before I sign the club accounts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell you the total.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My signature covers the receipts too. Let me check how it adds up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If you find a mistake, my name goes on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put mine beside yours. Give me the key and we'll correct it together before either name goes outside this room.

card.title: Steer the Suspicion
card.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That ink on your new sofa must be from the delivery label.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The label's dry. You signed with your fountain pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the driver brushed my signature against the fabric. We should photograph it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your pen's still leaking onto the cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The delivery must have cracked it when they squeezed past me. Photograph the pen too; that's a second claim.

card.title: Steer the Suspicion
card.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shelf fell because they supplied the wrong bracket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fitted it upside down. Look at the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a misleading arrow. We should photograph it for the manufacturer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew that arrow. I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because theirs was missing. Put that in the complaint; they made us supply our own safety markings.

card.title: A Kinder Version
card.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gallery thinks your portrait would suit a more adventurous exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're showing a fridge full of teeth. What did they say about mine?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That the face doesn't immediately reveal what you intended.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's you. They called it unrecognisable, didn't they?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They think knowing the sitter would help. I'll attend your next opening with a matching shirt.

card.title: A Kinder Version
card.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nina's keeping her birthday dinner small. You and I can get noodles.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Small? She invited the whole choir.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's choosing people she sees every week. It isn't a verdict on your friendship.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We rehearse together every Tuesday. Read me her message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She wants an uncomplicated evening. That's the kindest accurate sentence. Come have one with me.

card.title: Tell Me Why
card.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I once hid an invitation because I felt left out. Why hide mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'd have gone without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I nearly skipped your birthday when you invited Leah. Is this about being alone?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's about you liking her more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I counted your photos with her after that party. Did you hide mine to make me choose you?

card.title: Tell Me Why
card.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're circling the station. I avoid my old office too. Why this route?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My former boss catches this train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told mine I'd become a novelist. What did you tell yours?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That I had a better offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've carried the same blank notebook past mine for a year. Are you avoiding him because there wasn't a better offer?

card.title: Exactly as Planned
card.instruction: Treat every exposed flaw, failed step, and unexpected consequence as proof that the scheme is unfolding by design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The escape-room attendant found our shortcut. Phase one is working.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made me distract her so you could crawl through it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She was supposed to feel she'd caught us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's padlocked it. We've got two minutes left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The padlock rules out our decoy, and the deadline forces focus. Now we solve it exactly on schedule.

card.title: Exactly as Planned
card.instruction: Treat every exposed flaw, failed step, and unexpected consequence as proof that the scheme is unfolding by design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum found the surprise-party invitations. Right on schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made me hide them in my sock drawer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She had to feel she'd uncovered it herself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's cancelling the caterer. She hates surprises.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's her part of the plan: taking control. We surprise her with how completely we obey.

card.title: Outsmart the Room
card.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open the delivery email. Let me deduce where our office biscuits went.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for them. I'll tell everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait. That's a clue, not a conclusion. I should announce the solution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too late. They're downstairs opening the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them nobody eats until I identify the contents. Finding a box doesn't mean they've solved the biscuits.

card.title: Outsmart the Room
card.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my conclusion above yours on the board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're the same conclusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then chronology decides who outsmarted whom.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We spoke together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My chalk reached the board first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the drawer key. Yesterday it meant welcome; today it could explain the missing money.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You think it's evidence against me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It could become evidence for you if I can check the figures.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then take it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Let's see whether it can be an invitation again after the drawer opens.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A's changing interpretation of the key/note supports a continuing request to obtain it; the object stays the centre of the evidence and trust negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the original note. You called it a gift; now you use it as proof.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can read the relevant line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's become a verdict I can't inspect.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You may read all of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Perhaps the same paper can return to being something you trusted me with.

card.title: The Object Changes Meaning
card.instruction: Choose one ordinary detail and reinterpret it as gift, threat, evidence, or symbol as the scene evolves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave you that key because you were welcome here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then why are you holding it like evidence?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because the cupboard was locked before the cake disappeared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I brought you a replacement cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then perhaps the key is a subscription. We'll discuss the terms over tea.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

card.title: The Object Changes Meaning
card.instruction: Choose one ordinary detail and reinterpret it as gift, threat, evidence, or symbol as the scene evolves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep this old ticket. It proves we went somewhere together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It proves you booked us different trains.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's evidence of a mistake we survived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I kept my ticket too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put them together. Now they're an invitation to get it right.

card.title: Hand Over the Proof
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the drawer key so I can check the figures.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell you the total.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking how the total was built.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Don't you trust me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like the paperwork to share the responsibility.
